facts.text: No two snowflakes are exactly alike, and almost all of them have six sides.
Reindeer eyes change colour: golden in summer and deep blue in winter.
Candy canes were once plain white sticks. The red stripes came much later.
A real Christmas tree takes around eight years to grow.
The first decorated Christmas trees were hung with apples and nuts.
In Norway, people hide their brooms on Christmas Eve so witches can't borrow them!
In Czechia, some people cut a cherry branch on 4 December. If it blooms by Christmas, it's good luck!
Bells were rung at midwinter long ago to chase away the dark days.
A snowflake can take over an hour to fall from the clouds to your nose.
Polar bears have black skin under their fluffy fur.
In Iceland, thirteen funny Yule Lads visit one by one. One of them just loves to slam doors!
Gingerbread houses became popular after a famous fairy tale: Hansel and Gretel.
In Japan, a very popular Christmas dinner is fried chicken!
Both male and female reindeer can grow antlers.

activities.text: Draw a picture of your dream snowman. What is he wearing?
Fold a piece of paper, snip some shapes and unfold your very own snowflake.
Sing your favourite Christmas song as loud as you can. Then as quietly as you can!
Help a grown-up bake or decorate something yummy today.
Make a paper chain with one link for every sleep left until Christmas.
Build a blanket fort and read a story inside it with a torch.
Go on a walk and count how many Christmas trees you can spot in windows.
Make a Christmas card for someone who isn't expecting one.
Dance like a reindeer for one whole song. No giggling allowed!
Hide a tiny toy somewhere in the room and let your family hunt for it.
Put on your warmest socks and have a cosy family movie night.
Stick paper stars on your window to light the way for {bringer}.
Tell your family the silliest Christmas story you can make up.
Fill a jar with little notes about what you love about your family.

kindness.text: Give someone in your family a really big hug today.
Pick one toy you've outgrown and give it to a child who'd love it.
Help tidy up without anybody asking. Watch their faces!
Tell three people something you really like about them.
Put some seeds or crumbs outside for the winter birds.
Make someone laugh today. Your best joke, please!
Draw a picture for a grandparent or a neighbour.
Let someone else go first today, and smile while you do it.
